transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-08-21; Start: 16:00 UTC; Duration: 62 minutes; Location: All-hands (virtual)
Attendees: Avery Chen (CEO), Maya Patel (CTO), Jordan Lee (Head of Product), Samir Rao (VP Engineering), Priya Desai (Head of People), plus distributed engineering, product, sales and support.

Summary: (auto) Quick leadership touch to align on a small set of risks and decisions to carry into Q3. Not a full roadmap -- focus on Dedicated capacity ramp, private deployment readiness, ops tabletop and hiring risk.

Topics: Dedicated SLA, Private/VPC deployments, batching/quantization tradeoffs, hiring runway, incident exercises.

Transcript: [00:00] Avery Chen: Alright, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining the bridge meeting. We'll start on the agenda, I know it's a stretched week so short and focused.
[00:15] Maya Patel: Hi all. Quick note, there's a bit of background noise, sorry if you hear my kid in the background. Uh we're starting with the Dedicated capacity. Samir, do you want to lead?
[00:28] Samir Rao: Yeah sure. So we've been running the pilot clusters, the metrics look decent—throughput's within 10% of our targets but there's some variance at peak windows. The most common failure mode is the OOM during 4k token bursts, which I think is related to KV cash—kv cash sizing and a couple of model variants we tested. I think it's a mis-heard memory estimate on the nightly quantization jobs.
[00:54] Jordan Lee: Quick Q: when you say 10% variance what are we seeing versus SLA? Like p50/p95?
[01:05] Samir Rao: P50 is fine, p95 climbs to 420ms versus the SLA of 350ms under reserved capacity. Under contention we fall back to standard routing which increases latency unpredictably.
[01:20] Avery Chen: Are these contested windows correlated to any particular customer workloads? Any chance it's an A/B test leaking?
[01:28] Samir Rao: We dug in, it's a mix—some internal load testing, plus a couple large customers on burst policy. We'll isolate with staged isolation in the next rollout.
[01:38] Maya Patel: From product POV, the fallback behavior is intended but we need clearer SLO messaging to customers. We'll propose a canary schedule and also a customer-facing doc.
[01:51] Priya Desai: On the ops side we should flag that this may affect Dedicated sales pitches this quarter—need to be transparent with demo scripts.
[02:05] [noise, indistinct chatter]
[02:12] Jordan Lee: Next, private deployments: Maya?
[02:15] Maya Patel: Sure. The private control plane package is feature-complete for VPC onboarding but the install path has two documented steps that sometimes break on older kube versions. Our ops tests show a 15% failure in air-gapped installs which is higher than acceptable. We have a plan to backport the installer to 1.19 compatibility but that's nontrivial.
[02:39] Samir Rao: The main blocker is an init container that expects a newer netlink API. We can rewrite it but that's engineering time.
[02:46] Avery Chen: We need a decision: do we support backport for now or require customers to run a supported kube version? There's sales friction if we force upgrades.
[02:58] Maya Patel: Proposal: support 1.19/1.20 as a 'best effort' with documented caveats and charge a premium on on-prem projects requiring backports.
[03:12] Jordan Lee: Customers in regulated sectors will push for it, but we can gate it behind a services agreement.
[03:20] [crosstalk]
[03:25] Priya Desai: From hiring, if we anticipate more on-prem work we should add two infra contractors to handle installer/backport tasks for Q3; cheaper and faster than hiring perm.
[03:36] Avery Chen: Agree, please prepare a contractor requisition.
[03:40] [00:04]--note: timestamp ticks slightly misaligned due to manual entry--
[03:45] Avery Chen: On latency vs cost tradeoffs - Jordan you had a deck earlier about batching and quantization suggestions?
[03:54] Jordan Lee: Yeah, we ran internal experiments: enabling continuous batching on burst-heavy routes reduced per-token cost by ~18% but increased tail latency on single-user interactive sessions by 40ms. Quantization to 4-bit for some model families saves ~30% GPU memory and reduces cost but introduces occasional hallucination spikes in narrow evals. I'll share the evaluation harness with examples.
[04:20] Maya Patel: The ops concern is safety/regression monitoring. If we push quantized models into production for latency/cost, we need strong quality gates and canary prompts to detect regressions.
[04:33] Samir Rao: Also kernel selection and compilation plays into this; some of our kernels degrade on certain sequence length mixes. We should add sequence-length distribution checks during compile time.
[04:46] Avery Chen: Okay, action there: Jordan and Maya to define quality gates and a short checklist per model family.
[04:54] Jordan Lee: Will do.
[04:58] [05:00] Audience question (someone muted): Can you discuss the SLA guarantee for Dedicated versus Hosted?
[05:06] Avery Chen: Hosted keeps best-effort and lower cost; Dedicated is reserved capacity with stronger SLA on latency and uptime—still refining numbers but expecting 99.9% availability for committed pools. Pricing will reflect the reserved capacity.
[05:22] Maya Patel: We'll circulate the draft SLA by next week for feedback.
[05:30] [05:40] Priya Desai: Quick HR note—hiring runway: we have headroom for two IC hires in platform but budget approvals are pending. If we can't get perm hires approved we will start contractors as earlier suggested. Also reminders for the Q3 all-staff offsite sign-up.
[05:58] Avery Chen: On budget, my ask to the execs—identify low-impact features we can pause to free up 0.5 FTE equivalent funding for the infra push.
[06:14] Maya Patel: We'll review the roadmap and mark items 'deferable'.
[06:20] [06:30] Samir Rao: Ops tabletop: I'd like to propose a simulated incident drill focused on fallback routing and capacity exhaustion. We need to run this before we ramp Dedicated sales.
[06:42] Jordan Lee: Suggestion: Sept 10 for a two-hour session, include AE/Sales, SEs, SREs, and customer success. Make it scenario-based with a postmortem template.
[06:54] Priya Desai: I'll schedule and arrange facilitators.
[06:58] Avery Chen: Good. Also, we got some inbound from a big customer asking for a private pilot next month. We need to ensure the security packet and SOC2 attachments are ready. Maya, can you confirm?
[07:12] Maya Patel: SOC2 docs are up to date; however our privacy pack for private deployments needs an addendum describing KMS/HSM integration and audit log retention. I'll draft that.
[07:24] Samir Rao: We should include sample architecture diagrams for on-prem with HSM—some of the customers asked for offline key rotation details.
[07:33] Jordan Lee: Also note: billing and metering for private deployments—customers want per-model billing. We need to ensure the console exposes token-level breakdowns for private installs or at least provide a CSV export.
[07:47] Maya Patel: Agreed, product will prioritize CSV export for private first.
[07:53] [08:00] Audience comment: There's a user asking about partner integrations—any update with the cloud marketplace?
[08:05] Avery Chen: Marketplace listing is in progress—legal reviewing the terms. Should go live by end of month.
[08:12] [08:20] Jordan Lee: Quick FYI—we saw a 12% increase in usage on the hosted API after the model catalog refresh; that's promising for self-serve funnel.
[08:30] Maya Patel: That matches the telemetry that shows increased short session traffic—likely due to improved latency on common routes.
[08:38] [08:45] Priya Desai: Scheduling note: we'll do town halls monthly until the end of the year, shorter cadence. We'll also share docs in the weekly digest.
[08:55] Avery Chen: Ok to wrap. Quick recap?
[09:00] Jordan Lee: Recap: Jordan/Maya will deliver model quality gates and runbook; Samir will draft Dedicated rollout schedule; Priya will start contractor req and schedule the tabletop; Maya to publish privacy/security addendum; Jordan to finish Q3 OKRs.
[09:18] Maya Patel: Also SLA draft next week.
[09:22] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the #leadership channel and tag action owners. Meeting adjourned.

Action items (auto): Samir - Dedicated schedule; Maya - Private runbook and privacy addendum; Jordan - OKRs + quality gates; Priya - contractor req + schedule tabletop.

Notes on transcription: several words transcribed incorrectly (e.g., 'KV cache' as 'KV cash', 'VPC' as 'V-P-C'), some timestamps approximate, minor crosstalk present.

End of transcript.
